extract:
The Beatles were an English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960, active until their breakup in 1970. The classic lineup was John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr. They emerged from the city's Merseybeat scene, honing their act in the clubs of Hamburg, West Germany, and at Liverpool's Cavern Club. They became the central force of the British Invasion and are widely regarded as the most influential act in popular music history.

The group grew out of Lennon's skiffle band the Quarrymen, which McCartney joined in 1957 and Harrison in 1958. Their early influences included American rock and roll and R&B artists such as Elvis Presley, Chuck Berry, Little Richard, Buddy Holly and the Everly Brothers, along with Motown and girl-group records. Stuart Sutcliffe and drummer Pete Best were early members. After Brian Epstein became their manager in 1962, they signed to EMI's Parlophone label under producer George Martin, and Starr replaced Best that August. Their debut single "Love Me Do" was followed by "Please Please Me," which launched their run of British chart success.

Their 1963 albums Please Please Me and With The Beatles mixed Lennon-McCartney originals with covers such as "Twist and Shout." "I Want to Hold Your Hand" opened the American market, and their February 1964 appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show ignited Beatlemania in the United States. A Hard Day's Night (1964), the soundtrack to Richard Lester's film, was their first album of entirely original songs. Beatles For Sale and Help! (1965) followed, the latter containing "Yesterday." Rubber Soul (1965) marked a turn toward introspective songwriting and new textures, including Harrison's sitar on "Norwegian Wood." Revolver (1966) pushed further with tape loops on "Tomorrow Never Knows" and the string octet of "Eleanor Rigby." After they quit touring in 1966, studio work became their focus. Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band (1967), engineered with Geoff Emerick, became a landmark of psychedelic rock, alongside the "Strawberry Fields Forever"/"Penny Lane" single and Magical Mystery Tour. The double album The Beatles (1968), known as the White Album, ranged from "Helter Skelter" to "While My Guitar Gently Weeps." Yellow Submarine (1969) accompanied the animated film. Abbey Road (1969), featuring Harrison's "Something" and "Here Comes the Sun," was their last recorded album, while Let It Be, produced in its released form by Phil Spector, came out in 1970.

In 1968 they founded their own company, Apple Corps, and released records through Apple Records. Their contemporaries and rivals included the Rolling Stones, the Beach Boys and Bob Dylan. Dylan's influence shaped their lyrics, while Brian Wilson's Pet Sounds spurred the ambitions behind Sgt. Pepper. Their study with the Maharishi Mahesh Yogi in India in 1968 yielded much of the White Album, and keyboardist Billy Preston played on their late sessions, including the 1969 rooftop concert.

The Beatles are the best-selling music act of all time, with a record number of UK and US number-one singles. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1988. Their work reshaped the album as an art form, studio production and the image of the self-contained, songwriting rock band. After the split, all four pursued solo careers. Lennon was murdered in 1980 and Harrison died in 2001. The Anthology project of the mid-1990s revived interest in the band, as did the 2009 remasters and Giles Martin's anniversary remixes beginning with Sgt. Pepper. Peter Jackson's 2021 documentary Get Back offered a new view of their final era, and in 2023 "Now and Then," completed using machine-learning audio separation of a Lennon demo, became billed as the final Beatles song.
title: The Beatles
